data.description: Enchanting is a game mechanic unlocked after defeating Supreme Witch, Calamitas, which allows the player to apply enchantments to their items, granting them unique additional qualities. It changes the name of an item by adding a prefix to the item's name (before any modifier the item may have), such...

				<h1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading mw-first-heading"><span class="mw-page-title-main">Enchantment</span></h1>
				<div id="bodyContent" class="vector-body">
					<div id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Calamity Mod Wiki</div>
					<div id="contentSub"></div>
					<div id="contentSub2"></div>
					
					<div id="jump-to-nav"></div>
					<a class="mw-jump-link" href="#mw-head">Jump to navigation</a>
					<a class="mw-jump-link" href="#searchInput">Jump to search</a>
					<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><div class="infobox item float-right" style="width:12em;;"><div class="title">Enchantment</div><div class="section images"><ul class="inline"><li><a href="/wiki/File:All_Enchantments.gif" class="image"><img alt="All Enchantments.gif" src="/images/All_Enchantments.gif?2815d7" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="38" height="38" data-file-width="38" data-file-height="38"></a></li></ul></div><div class="section statistics"><table class="stat"></table></div></div>
<p><b>Enchanting</b> is a game mechanic unlocked after defeating <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Witch,_Calamitas" title="Supreme Witch, Calamitas">Supreme Witch, Calamitas</a>, which allows the player to apply <b>enchantments</b> to their items, granting them unique additional qualities. It changes the name of an item by adding a prefix to the item's name (before any <a href="/wiki/Modifier" class="mw-redirect" title="Modifier">modifier</a> the item may have), such as "Aflame Strong <a href="/wiki/Photon_Ripper" title="Photon Ripper">Photon Ripper</a>." Hovering the cursor over an item with an enchantment in an inventory slot will show the enchantment details beneath the item's description. This description is colored <span style="color:#8B0000; font-weight:bold;">#8B0000</span>. Additionally, the name of an enchanted item will visually pulse outwards approximately once per second.
</p><p>Unlike modifiers, enchantments are qualitative in nature; rather than solely providing stat boosts, enchantments usually cause effects to occur upon use of the item. Each enchantment has an upside and a downside — there are no enchantments that are solely beneficial.
</p><p>A select few items have access to the unique "<b><a href="#Exhume">Exhume</a></b>" enchantment, which transforms the provided item into an entirely new item.
</p>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Enchanting">Enchanting</span></h2>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:322px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Enchantment_Curse_Background.png" class="image"><img src="/images/thumb/Enchantment_Curse_Background.png/320px-Enchantment_Curse_Background.png?d156b2" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="320" height="264" class="thumbimage" srcset="/images/Enchantment_Curse_Background.png?d156b2 1.5x" data-file-width="392" data-file-height="324"></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Enchantment_Curse_Background.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The Enchantment interface when interacting with the Brimstone Witch.</div></div></div>
<p>Enchanting is a service provided by the <a href="/wiki/Brimstone_Witch" title="Brimstone Witch">Brimstone Witch</a>, which applies an enchantment of the player's choosing to an item in exchange for <a href="/wiki/Coins" class="mw-redirect" title="Coins">coins</a>. This enchantment can be removed at any time by placing the item into the enchanting interface and selecting "Disenchant." The disenchanting process costs the same amount of money that it cost to enchant the item with the enchantment that is being removed. Upon disenchanting the item, the player is free to select a new enchantment.
</p><p>The Brimstone Witch charges 10 times an item's <a href="https://terraria.wiki.gg/wiki/Value" class="extiw" title="tgc:Value">sell value</a> in order to enchant or disenchant it. This price can be lowered by <a href="/wiki/Brimstone_Witch#Living_preferences" title="Brimstone Witch">happiness</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Discount_Card" class="mw-redirect" title="Discount Card">Discount Card</a> and its upgrade, the <a href="/wiki/Greedy_Ring" class="mw-redirect" title="Greedy Ring">Greedy Ring</a>.
</p><p>Enchanting can be accessed by talking to the Brimstone Witch and choosing "Enchant" from the options (upon opening this option for the first time, she will give the player a <a href="/wiki/Brimstone_Locus" title="Brimstone Locus">Brimstone Locus</a>). The player can then insert the item to be enchanted into the interface that appears below the inventory. Next to the item slot is a small key that, when clicked, enchants the item with the selected enchantment in the box on the right. The selected enchantment can be changed by clicking the arrows on the top and bottom of the box.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Enchantments">Enchantments</span></h2>
<p>Enchantments can be applied to most items, with the exception being consumable weapons. Like modifiers, certain enchantments are exclusive to certain classes or types of items due to what they affect. For example, Oblatory is a magic-exclusive enchantment, as it deals with mana. 
</p>

<p>This value starts at 1600, decreases every time the enchanted weapon is used, and tries to increase by 1 every frame (60 per second), meaning it takes 26.66 seconds for the exhaustion bar to rejuvenate back to maximum damage from being fully empty. The decrease upon use is determined by the use time of the weapon; the value will decrease by the weapon's use time multiplied by 2.25, with a lower cap of 10. For example, <a href="/wiki/Sacrifice" title="Sacrifice">Sacrifice</a>'s use time of 8 would decrease the value by 18 on each usage; <a href="/wiki/Helium_Flash" title="Helium Flash">Helium Flash</a>'s use time of 40 will decrease the value by 90 on each usage. The value cannot become a negative number.
</p><p>The damage of weapons enchanted with Ephemeral is increased by 1.26x by default. As the weapon is used and the exhaustion value decreases, damage variance ("exhaustion") is introduced, causing the damage to sink to a potential minimum value of 0.77x. The exact multiplier is determined by the function <code> lerp(0.77, 1.26, 2 ^ exhaustion ratio - 1) </code>, where the exhaustion ratio is the current exhaustion divided by 1600. Depending on the value of 2<sup>exhaustion ratio</sup> - 1, the multiplier is linearly divided between 0.77x and 1.26x. For example, if the value was 0 (at an exhaustion ratio of 0) then the multiplier would be 0.77x; if the value was 1 (at an exhaustion ratio of 1) then the multiplier would be 1.26x; if the value was 0.414 (at an exhaustion ratio of 0.5) then the multiplier would be ~0.97x.

<td>Hellbound</td>
<td>Causes minions to be created with a 40 second timer. Once it runs out, they explode violently. Minions do more damage the longer they live and idly explode as well.</td>
<td><div class="center"><div class="floatnone"><a href="/wiki/File:Enchantment_Rune_Hellbound.png" class="image"><img alt="Enchantment Rune Hellbound.png" src="/images/Enchantment_Rune_Hellbound.png?93a32a" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="28" height="36" data-file-width="28" data-file-height="36"></a></div></div></td>

<td>Any <a href="/wiki/Minion" class="mw-redirect" title="Minion">minion</a> summoned by the enchanted weapon will <span class="i"><img alt="Brimstone Explosion" src="/images/Brimstone_Explosion.gif?d7ec09" decoding="async" loading="lazy" title="Brimstone Explosion" width="44" height="46" data-file-width="44" data-file-height="46"></span> explode after 40 seconds and subsequently despawn.
<p>Based on a ratio completion of the 40 second timer, minions can do between 1x and 1.6x damage. This is not a linear increase; the damage gain will increase slower if the timer has just started or is about to end, and will increase faster in the middle of the timer.
</p><p>Every 40 frames (0.667 seconds) there is a 1/12 (8.33%) chance for the minion to cause an explosion (although this will not cause them to be desummoned) with a base of 2000 damage. When the countdown is at 5 seconds or less, fireball sounds and fire dust will appear on the minion, signifying that it is close to exploding (and subsequently despawning).
</p><p>Upon the countdown reaching 0 seconds, the minions will explode (and despawn) with a base of 6000 damage. Both explosions are affected by minion damage boosts.
</p>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Notes">Notes</span></h2>
<ul><li>Unlike modifiers, enchantments do not change the <a href="/wiki/Value" class="mw-redirect" title="Value">value</a> or <a href="/wiki/Rarity" title="Rarity">rarity</a> of a weapon.</li>
<li>The Community is the only <a href="/wiki/Accessory" class="mw-redirect" title="Accessory">accessory</a> that can be enchanted, and its only available enchantment is Exhumed.</li>
<li>Certain items are restricted from receiving specific enchantments:
<ul><li>The <a href="/wiki/Eternity" title="Eternity">Eternity</a> cannot receive the Oblatory enchantment.</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/The_Final_Dawn" title="The Final Dawn">The Final Dawn</a> cannot receive the Resentful or Bloodthirsty enchantments.</li>
<li>The <a href="/wiki/Heavenly_Gale" title="Heavenly Gale">Heavenly Gale</a> cannot receive the Ephemeral enchantment.</li></ul></li></ul>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Trivia">Trivia</span></h2>
<ul><li>The word "exhume" means to dig something up from being buried, especially from a grave. This fits the theme of necromancy that is present in the Exhumed items.</li>
<li>Exhume's rune (to the right of the enchantment name box) is the only rune to be purple, rather than red like the other enchantments.</li>
<li>The runes associated with each enchantment are <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:alchemical_symbol" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:alchemical symbol">alchemical symbols</a> for various things that are relevant to the concept of the enchantment.
<ul><li>Aflame uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:fire" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:fire">fire</a>, because of its effect to set both enemies and the player ablaze.</li>
<li>Ephemeral uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:air" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:air">air</a>, to represent the volatility of the enchantment. Additionally, physical <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:Fatique" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:Fatique">exhaustion</a> is often associated with heavy breathing and panting, which involve intake of air into the body.</li>
<li>Withering uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:salt" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:salt">salt</a>, which refers to the idea of "rubbing salt into a wound", a phrase meaning to cause more misfortune on something which has already experienced misfortune.</li>
<li>Resentful uses the alchemical symbol for the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:moon" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:moon">moon</a> because of its low gravity, which is similar to how the enchantment causes the weapon to deal more damage from further away.</li>
<li>Bloodthirsty uses the alchemical symbol for the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:sun" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:sun">sun</a> because of its high gravity, which is similar to how the enchantment causes the weapon to deal more damage up close.</li>
<li>Persecuted uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:sulfur" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:sulfur">sulfur</a>, as sulfur and demons are commonly found together in general mythology.</li>
<li>Lecherous uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:magnesium" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:magnesium">magnesium</a> because it is very difficult to extinguish once set on fire, and this causes it to be associated with eternity in alchemy. The Lecherous Orb that spawns is eternally present and can be considered to provide the player with eternal life through the hearts that it drops.</li>
<li>Tainted uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:death" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:death">death</a>, as it summons skeletal arms, and skeletons are heavily associated with death due to typically being the final state of a human or animal after postmortem decomposition.</li>
<li>Oblatory uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:lead" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:lead">lead</a>, as the enchantment's life-sapping effect can be compared to <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:lead_poisoning" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:lead poisoning">lead poisoning</a>.</li>
<li>Traitorous uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:Mercury_(element)" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:Mercury (element)">mercury</a>, an element that is useful but can cause considerable damage to one's body if handled improperly.</li>
<li>Indignant uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:ash" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:ash">ash</a>, because of the charred theme of the demons, and because <a href="/wiki/Demon" class="mw-redirect" title="Demon">demons</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ash_Block" class="mw-redirect" title="Ash Block">ash</a> are closely related in <i>Terraria</i>.</li>
<li>Hellbound uses the alchemical symbol for <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:potassium" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:potassium">potassium</a>, an element that is known to explode on contact with water.</li>
<li>Exhumed uses the alchemical symbol of the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:philosopher%27s_stone" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:philosopher's stone">philosopher's stone</a>. The philosopher's stone was fabled to be able to turn <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:base_metals" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:base metals">base metals</a> such as lead (considered common, impure, of little value) into <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:precious_metals" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:precious metals">precious metals</a> such as <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:gold" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:gold">gold</a> (considered rare, pure, of high value), similar to Exhume's ability to transform weaker items into ones with significantly greater power.</li></ul></li>
<li>The Withered debuff is a reference to a <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://minecraft.wiki/w/Wither_(effect)">status effect of the same name</a> from the game <i><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/en:Minecraft" class="extiw" title="wikipedia:en:Minecraft">Minecraft</a></i>, featuring an identical death message ("<PlayerName> withered away.") and a similar icon of a dark crumbling heart.</li>
<li>During development, enchantments were also known as "curses", due to their significant drawbacks.</li></ul>

<ul><li>Increased the damage of red demons from Persecuted against the player from 95 to 360 / <b><abbr class="expert_value" style="cursor:pointer;" title="Expert Mode">450</abbr></b> <span class="i"><a href="/wiki/Expert_Mode" title="Expert Mode"><img alt="Expert Mode" src="/images/thumb/Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/10px-Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?5f831a" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="10" height="15" srcset="/images/thumb/Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/15px-Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?5f831a 1.5x, /images/thumb/Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/20px-Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?5f831a 2x" data-file-width="26" data-file-height="38"></a></span> / <b><abbr class="master_value" style="cursor:pointer;" title="Master Mode">540</abbr></b> <span class="i"><a href="/wiki/Master_Mode" title="Master Mode"><img alt="Master Mode" src="/images/thumb/Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/10px-Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?83be4d" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="10" height="15" srcset="/images/thumb/Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/15px-Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?83be4d 1.5x, /images/thumb/Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/20px-Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?83be4d 2x" data-file-width="26" data-file-height="38"></a></span>.</li>
<li>Reworked Traitorous:
<ul><li>Now spawns a Mana Monster when below 25% of max mana, consuming all of the player's remaining mana.</li>
<li>The monster's damage is equal to 80x the amount of mana consumed, deals 360 / <b><abbr class="expert_value" style="cursor:pointer;" title="Expert Mode">450</abbr></b> <span class="i"><a href="/wiki/Expert_Mode" title="Expert Mode"><img alt="Expert Mode" src="/images/thumb/Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/10px-Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?5f831a" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="10" height="15" srcset="/images/thumb/Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/15px-Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?5f831a 1.5x, /images/thumb/Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/20px-Expert_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?5f831a 2x" data-file-width="26" data-file-height="38"></a></span> / <b><abbr class="master_value" style="cursor:pointer;" title="Master Mode">540</abbr></b> <span class="i"><a href="/wiki/Master_Mode" title="Master Mode"><img alt="Master Mode" src="/images/thumb/Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/10px-Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?83be4d" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="10" height="15" srcset="/images/thumb/Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/15px-Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?83be4d 1.5x, /images/thumb/Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png/20px-Master_Indicator_%28borderless%29.png?83be4d 2x" data-file-width="26" data-file-height="38"></a></span> damage to the player and inflicts Vulnerability Hex for 3 seconds to the player.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/2.0.1.002" title="2.0.1.002">2.0.1.002</a></b>: Added new enchanting and exhuming sounds.</li></ul>
<ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/2.0.1.001" title="2.0.1.001">2.0.1.001</a></b>: Indignant's healing orbs can now pass through tiles.</li></ul>
<ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/2.0.0.001" title="2.0.0.001">2.0.0.001</a></b>:
<ul><li>Ephemeral can no longer be applied to all rogue weapons.</li>
<li>Lecherous can no longer be applied to true melee weapons.</li>
<li>Resprited Weak Brimstone Flames. Previous sprite was <a href="/wiki/File:Weak_Brimstone_Flames_(1.5.0.001).png" class="image"><img alt="Weak Brimstone Flames (1.5.0.001).png" src="/images/Weak_Brimstone_Flames_%281.5.0.001%29.png?ebfb66" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="32" height="32" data-file-width="32" data-file-height="32"></a></li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/1.5.1.001" title="1.5.1.001">1.5.1.001</a></b>:
<ul><li>Ephemeral can no longer be applied to channeled weapons.</li>
<li>Indignant's Demon, Exhumed Brimstone Heart, Lecherous Orb, and Prosecuted's Mysterious Portal are now vulnerable to cold and water debuffs, but resistant to heat debuffs.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/1.5.0.002" title="1.5.0.002">1.5.0.002</a></b>:
<ul><li>Added line splits to all tooltips.</li>
<li>Fixed a sprite error on the Withered debuff.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/1.5.0.001" title="1.5.0.001">1.5.0.001</a></b>: Introduced.</li></ul>
</div></div>
